Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 07/14/2026
Patient: Felton Conroy, 82-year-old male

Subjective:
Mr. Conroy presents for his routine follow-up visit. He reports feeling generally well with no new complaints today.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurological exams are unremarkable.

Assessment:
Mr. Conroy remains in good health for his age with no new issues identified during this visit.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine health maintenance. Encourage regular exercise and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/09/2026
Patient: Felton Conroy, 82-year-old male

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/09/2026: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Approximately 30% loss of T12 vertebral body height.

Impression:
There is an acute compression fracture involving the T12 vertebral body characterized by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. The vertebral body height is reduced by approximately 30% at this level.

No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracic or lumbar spine on this study.

notes.title: Spine Intervention Consultation
notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/12/2026
Patient: Felton Conroy, 82-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 07/05/2026 after a fall from standing height, 10 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 7/10 despite 9 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and calcitonin nasal spray, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 23/24.

Assessment:
Persistent moderate back pain related to vertebral fracture sustained 10 weeks ago. Despite conservative treatment, pain remains significant with high disability score.

Plan:
Discussed options for spine intervention to improve pain control and function. Patient to consider interventional procedures and follow-up in 4 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.
